title: What are all mechanisms to resolve multiple beans of the same type (@Primary, @Qualifier, variable name, List/Map injection, @Profile, custom qualifier)? When does NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException occur? What is the difference between @Primary and @Qualifier?
shortTitle: How do you resolve multiple beans of the same type?

s1_definition.profdef: When Spring finds multiple beans of the same type, it cannot decide which to inject and throws `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException`. Resolution mechanisms (priority order): `@Qualifier("name")` on injection point (explicit, highest), `@Primary` on bean definition (default fallback), field/parameter name matching bean name (implicit), `List<T>`/`Map<String,T>` injection (all beans), `@Profile` (environment-specific). `@Primary` says "I am the default." `@Qualifier` says "I want this specific one." `@Qualifier` overrides `@Primary`.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank has Email, SMS, and Push notification channels. When TransferService asks for "a NotificationService," Spring sees three candidates and panics. @Primary marks email as the default (most services want email). @Qualifier("sms") explicitly picks SMS for urgent fraud alerts. List injection gets ALL channels for marketing broadcasts.
s1_definition.oneliner: @Primary = default when no qualifier. @Qualifier = explicit pick by name. List/Map = get all. Without any: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** When Spring finds multiple beans of the same type, it cannot decide which to inject and throws `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException`. Resolution mechanisms (priority order): `@Qualifier("name")` on injection point (explicit, highest), `@Primary` on bean definition (default fallback), field/parameter name matching bean name (implicit), `List<T>`/`Map<String,T>` injection (all beans), `@Profile` (environment-specific). `@Primary` says "I am the default." `@Qualifier` says "I want this specific one." `@Qualifier` overrides `@Primary`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The bank has Email, SMS, and Push notification channels. When TransferService asks for "a NotificationService," Spring sees three candidates and panics. @Primary marks email as the default (most services want email). @Qualifier("sms") explicitly picks SMS for urgent fraud alerts. List injection gets ALL channels for marketing broadcasts.

**One line to remember:** @Primary = default when no qualifier. @Qualifier = explicit pick by name. List/Map = get all. Without any: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.

sections.s2_technical:
Resolution order: (1) `@Qualifier` match, (2) `@Primary`, (3) parameter/field name match, (4) single candidate. None resolves = exception.

**@Primary:** on the bean definition — "I am the default."
**@Qualifier:** on the injection point — "I want this specific one." Overrides @Primary.
**List/Map injection:** `List<NotificationService>` gets all. `Map<String, NotificationService>` keys = bean names — runtime selection.
**Custom qualifier:** `@PrimaryChannel` / `@FallbackChannel` — semantic, self-documenting annotations.
sections.s3_banking:
**Problem — The bank has three notification channels (Email, SMS, Push).** TransferService needs email by default. FraudAlertService needs SMS for urgency. MarketingService needs ALL channels for broadcast campaigns. CustomerPreferenceService needs to pick the channel at runtime based on the customer's saved preference.

**What the project will show:** Three NotificationService implementations, @Primary for default, @Qualifier for specific, List for fan-out, Map for runtime selection, custom qualifier annotations, and @Profile for environment-specific beans.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Spring scans and finds 3 NotificationService implementations: Email (@Primary), SMS, Push. Registers all three as singleton beans.

**Step 2.** TransferNotifier needs NotificationService with no qualifier. Spring picks @Primary = EmailNotificationService. Transfer confirmations go via email.

**Step 3.** FraudAlertNotifier has @Qualifier("smsNotificationService"). Spring ignores @Primary and directly picks SmsNotificationService. Urgent fraud alerts go via SMS.

**Step 4.** MarketingBroadcaster has `List<NotificationService>`. Spring collects all 3 beans into the list. Marketing campaigns broadcast through email + SMS + push simultaneously.

**Step 5.** CustomerPreferenceNotifier has `Map<String, NotificationService>`. Keys are bean names. At runtime, it reads customer preference from DB ("smsNotificationService" for Priya) and picks the matching channel dynamically.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Spring Container — 3 beans of type NotificationService:
    ├─ emailNotificationService (@Primary)
    ├─ smsNotificationService
    └─ pushNotificationService

  ═══ INJECTION RESOLUTION ═══

  TransferNotifier(NotificationService notifier)      ← no @Qualifier
    └─ Resolution: @Primary wins → emailNotificationService (Recommended) 

  FraudAlertNotifier(@Qualifier("smsNotificationService") NotificationService sms)
    └─ Resolution: @Qualifier overrides @Primary → smsNotificationService (Recommended) 

  MarketingBroadcaster(List<NotificationService> all)
    └─ Resolution: ALL beans → [email, sms, push] (Recommended) 

  CustomerPreferenceNotifier(Map<String, NotificationService> map)
    └─ Resolution: ALL beans keyed by name → {
         "emailNotificationService": email,
         "smsNotificationService": sms,
         "pushNotificationService": push
       } (Recommended) 

  ═══ RUNTIME ═══

  Transfer completed (SAV2001 → CUR3001 Rs.50000):
    TransferNotifier → EMAIL → "Transfer Confirmation"

  Fraud detected (TRD-SUSPICIOUS):
    FraudAlertNotifier → SMS → "URGENT: Suspicious activity"

  Diwali campaign:
    MarketingBroadcaster → EMAIL + SMS + PUSH → "0% brokerage offer!"

  Priya's statement (preference=SMS):
    CustomerPreferenceNotifier → Map.get("smsNotificationService") → SMS
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
When Spring finds multiple beans of the same type, it throws NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. The resolution mechanisms in priority order are: Qualifier on the injection point which explicitly names the bean, Primary on the bean definition which marks the default, field or parameter name matching a bean name as an implicit qualifier, and finally single-candidate resolution when only one bean exists. Qualifier always overrides Primary. Primary goes on the bean definition and says "I am the default." Qualifier goes on the injection point and says "I want this specific one."

In my banking notification gateway, we have three NotificationService implementations: email marked as Primary because most services want email, SMS, and push. The transfer confirmation service receives the Primary email bean automatically. The fraud alert service uses Qualifier to explicitly request SMS for urgent security alerts that need immediate delivery. The marketing broadcaster injects a List of all NotificationService beans to broadcast campaigns through every channel simultaneously. The customer preference service injects a Map keyed by bean name and selects the channel at runtime based on the customer's saved preference in the database. This Map injection pattern is particularly powerful for runtime dispatch because it avoids if-else chains and makes adding a new channel as simple as creating a new Service bean — no existing code changes needed.
